The complete journey, from elevation fields to streets, and from parcels to roofs. What the code computes, why it computes it, which sources inform it — and what its results do not establish.

A traceable explanation, not a certification.

Magna Urbis creates landscapes and settlements for maps and tabletop role-playing games. It combines established algorithms, numerical adaptations and artistic heuristics. A plausible-looking river is not a hydrological forecast; a medina plan is not an archaeological reconstruction; a requested population is not a population actually housed.

This page connects the stages. Method notes and source code remain the detailed references. “Code” links point to the online repository; the paths and SHA-256 fingerprints recorded in the inspected checkout are retained in
. Online branches may change after this inspection. Screenshots are unretouched project files; their age and evidential scope are stated.
A function or execution path exists in the repository. This does not guarantee every configuration or exhaustive visual validation.
A local design choice, parameter set or original combination. The algorithm and its assumptions are explained; no paper is cited as artificial authority.
A publication that helps place the method in context, without claiming a complete reimplementation.

retains its world generation, cultures and rendering. The Rust pipeline separates retained terrain, settlement placement, roads and urban stages. Workshop interfaces and TypeScript bridges orchestrate these computations. The Rust house engine has its own catalogue and solver; urban placement now calls it. This connection is real, but individual houses may be refused, and large ensembles still require validation.

In some files, “V2” also names a rendering style. A V2 visual option alone therefore does not establish that generation uses the complete new workflow. Evidence must identify the engine, backend and applied state.

. The second screen separates placement and roads from individual or collective construction. The workflow can also run in one click. Retained terrain and hydrology are preserved while places are built or modified.

. These historical captures document the classic workflow. The current version starts with Rust: structured forms forward terrain, neural model, erosion, climate and hydrology settings to the selected engine. Native terrain, physical fields and the water network are retained together; they are no longer replaced with fresh TypeScript drainage. Rust settlement placement and roads reuse this territory, followed by staged urban generation. The classic engine remains separately selectable. Width and the eight sea directions can be configured before the first calculation, with Rust widths from 500 m to 100 km. Always record the backend actually applied at each stage.

The V2 Rust urban integration provides four explicit stages:
replays exercised all four stages through accepted houses. The TypeScript screenshots above remain attributed to their own workflow; they are not images of those Rust tests.

Settings may be global or specific to a place, then target a quarter, parcel or identified house request. Reports expose warnings and refusals; refused requests can be retried with corrected configurations. Overrides remain subject to recipes and physical constraints. A local request counter allows checking that a house edit does not implicitly rerun terrain generation or the entire cadastre.

The logical sequence is terrain → water → settlements → roads → town → programme and parcels → buildings → presentation. Feedback and local iterations also occur: the programme reserves land before subdivision; the built balance is reconciled after actual placements. Downstream stages consume applied data, including geometries, holes, identities and refusals.
Original explanatory dependency diagram. Boxes describe responsibilities rather than the exact buttons of an interface.
Coordinates and elevation: metres. Area: m². Slope: vertical rise / horizontal distance. Temperature: °C; rainfall: mm/year.
Culture, period, population, function, known resources, navigability and lore are explicit intentions. Missing data does not become an established fact.
Surfaces, graphs and scenes can be reused. Changing the camera or style need not rerun erosion or house solving.
A slope of 0.12 means 12%, or approximately 6.84°. The conversion is
. Gross density in inhabitants per hectare includes streets and open space; it is distinct from the density of residential parcels alone.

An edited interface field may be a draft. Exports and evidence must identify the configuration that actually produced the scene. Crops translate geometries into their new frame; physical elevations, normals and dimensions are not multiplied by the display’s vertical exaggeration.
Combining projects: a territory or a recipe
Full import preserves the supplied scene. Composition offers two narrower operations.

adopts its physical grids, sea, rivers and lakes without recomputing terrain or hydrology, while retaining the current urban recipe. Previous sites, roads, towns and geometric edits are discarded: they must be rebuilt on this territory.

instead retains the current territory and imports the other project’s intentions: population, cultures, placement, morphology and declared overrides. Foreign terrain and town geometries are not transplanted. Settings keyed by stable identities belong to the recipe; manual edits to an old building footprint do not have that scope and are not merged.

If the file’s settings are a draft inconsistent with its displayed map, the retained surface becomes a portable FP32 input; the applied biome and computation provenance remain those of the territory. The operation rebuilds natural cover and layers that depended on the removed towns, without claiming to preserve previous agricultural occupation. Composition runs in a worker. The

checks, among other things, the preserved physical fingerprint, removal of obsolete geometry, caching and rebuilding after composition; it does not prove that every recipe is automatically valid on every site.
The TypeScript generator distributes randomness through named sub-seeds (
). This separation allows terrain reuse when only urban options change. It does not imply that two engines, versions or GPU backends always produce identical bits.
Seed, map width, relief family, motif size, blending and erosion/coast settings.
2D simplex noise, octaves, domain warping, finite landforms and retained corrections.
A signed elevation field in metric coordinates; a surface that subsequent stages can sample.

Coherent noise varies continuously in space: nearby points generally receive similar values. The engine combines several frequencies and amplitudes, then warps the evaluation coordinates. An explanatory formulation is:
the domain displacement. Long wavelengths structure the main landmasses; shorter wavelengths carry detail. The local code uses simplex noise:
places this family of constructions in context, but is not an exact description of the implementation.

Map size and motif size have distinct roles. Plains, hills, valleys, mountains, plateaus, canyons, volcanoes and calderas add their own structures. Finite landforms have a position and spatial support; open terrain is evaluated in regional coordinates. Coastal environments produce elevations below and above sea level. This treatment constructs landscape forms; it does not simulate tectonic plates.

The Rust source field uses, among other settings, an internal resolution of 1024². The retained surface and local treatments allow sampling a region without restarting erosion. Filtering excessively fine octaves limits aliasing; oversampling a coarse surface does not add geological observations.
“Fractal”, “geological” and “natural” describe constructions or visual families here. None of these labels establishes a measured stratigraphic history, lithology or geological age.
Terrain Diffusion and the finite window.

, by Alexander Goslin, makes diffusion sampling lazy and unbounded. Terrain Diffusion applies the algorithm to terrain. Windows use spatially coherent noise and weighted overlaps; they are not independently generated tiles stitched together. The properties of the published algorithm do not automatically become properties of every application that uses its weights.
In Magna Urbis, the documented workflow produces a
. The planner works backwards from the delivered region to determine the required windows:
Regional context, conditioned on a sketch and climate.
Latent field conditioned on the coarse stage.
Reconstruction of detail and elevation; resampling for the workshop.

→ original base in one evaluation → distilled student decoder is a local configuration, with backend variants. The sketch controls large landforms; a depression smaller than the coarse grid is not guaranteed to survive. The imported surface retains its provenance and is not subjected again to procedural erosion and coastal cutting. Hydrology follows.
The network, its conditioning and the method that evolves it from noise are three distinct objects.
can learn generation with few evaluations. This does not justify arbitrarily turning a multistep model into a single-pass model.

Browser mode uses Rust/WASM and WebGPU with external, cached weights; Python mode uses PyTorch/CUDA. Quantisation and precision may differ. Two visually similar outputs do not prove numerical equivalence. Replay evidence must fix the weights and backend.

in V2: they require WebGPU in the browser or local Python/CUDA. Neural requests with CPU computation are explicitly refused; they are not silently replaced with procedural noise. CPU computation remains available for procedural terrain and Rust urban generation.
Neural Earth is a separate project

It connects Orogen’s planetary context to learned refinement. Adding Magna Urbis towns to that pipeline remains an integration goal. Sharing a neural engine does not establish that a town is already integrated into a planet.

constructs a drainage potential from outlets by processing cells in increasing elevation order. A depression’s spill elevation indicates how water could escape; it does not mean that the entire physical ground must be raised to that elevation.

evaluates triangular facets around a cell and distributes contributing area between two downstream neighbours. It reduces the bias of D8’s eight fixed directions. The final vector network has its own topology: the area partition used for incision is not the geometry of a drawn river.
This equation places the incision model in context. The implicit solver of

handles the downstream dependency of elevations. The local implementation adapts it for interactivity: capped contributing area, a weaker response on gentle slopes, and bounded incision and corrections. The erosion slider controls intensity, with no established conversion into thousands of years.

The engine supplements incision with controlled threshold breaching, basin filling, thermal relaxation beyond the talus slope and hillslope diffusion. These passes modify different aspects of the terrain. Advanced settings expose iterations, incision, slope thresholds, filling, breaching, talus, diffusion and surface treatments. GPU paths use dedicated shaders; their presence does not guarantee bitwise identity with CPU results.
What the computation does not retain as a complete simulation

The project does not provide a generally calibrated sediment-mass balance, 2D/3D hydraulics, coupled tectonics or a physical geological duration here. Hillslope diffusion and the neural diffusion of the preceding chapter are distinct mechanisms.
Retained elevations, sea, resolution, temperature, rainfall and hydrological constraints.
Drainage and flats → basins → lake balance → river graph and profiles → beds and surfaces.
No downstream loops; connected confluences; water compatible with the ground and permitted corrections.

Flow directions and contributing areas structure a network. Flat areas require a topological ordering, because slope alone does not define a downstream direction. Retained depressions become lakes; others may receive a breach or bounded correction. Initial diagnostics remain distinct from final corrections.
Original conceptual cross-section, not to scale. The elevation required for drainage, the physical ground and the water surface are three distinct quantities.
The lake balance is simplified and explicit
The local module computes potential evaporation using elevation-adjusted temperature, followed by an empirical annual evapotranspiration:

Runoff floors are generator choices, not natural laws. At equilibrium, catchment inflow approximately balances evaporation from the lake surface. If inflow exceeds evaporation from a full lake, it spills over the threshold and passes on the excess. The module draws inspiration from
; it does not reproduce the paper’s entire dynamic hierarchy.

Sources, reaches, confluences and outlets become connected objects. Shared nodes preserve junctions. Width, bed and water profiles are evaluated along centre lines with correction budgets. Meanders add deterministic, multiscale variations constrained by terrain; this is not a complete time-dependent simulation of lateral migration.

A conservative obstacle mask may widen a river for route finding. It must not be mistaken for the drawn bank or physical width. Vegetation rendering therefore uses the displayed water surfaces. This distinction is decisive for narrow rivers and cropped regions.
the exact annual balance shown above
Buildability comes before the town’s name.

Settlement placement evaluates dry candidates using slope, freshwater access, coastline, defence, declared preferences and the space actually available. A favourable point is insufficient: population implies a usable footprint, and footprints must respect exclusions and spacing. Candidate ranks and scores can be retained for inspection.
Rank–size mode distributes populations according to

, with a minimum threshold and a settlement density over usable land. This is a demographic distribution control. The engine does not demonstrate the historical emergence of Zipf’s law from economic exchange.

Rust screenshot already present in the repository: tropical island, settlement locations and regional network. Named points are not houses. The exact recipe and commit for this older screenshot are not supplied in its source folder; it illustrates the stage without establishing complete reproducibility.

A riverside site is not automatically a navigable harbour. An unknown resource remains unknown. Site data subsequently informs the programme and countryside, without inventing an economy from a colour or cultural name.
A network of links, then physical paths.

The engine selects links between settlements on a Delaunay graph, retains a spanning backbone and adds shortcuts. This demand graph states which places to connect; it is not yet the physical route geometry.

Path search minimises a cost that depends on terrain, gradients, obstacles, turns and reuse of existing roads. State includes the arrival direction: a turn has a cost that depends on the preceding movement. A wider range of moves than the eight neighbouring cells limits rigid trajectories and allows switchbacks. Intersections are then assembled into a planar graph.
This formulation is an explanatory breakdown, not a copy of the coefficients.

provides the reference for this family of anisotropic shortest paths. Magna Urbis road classes, thresholds and crossings are local adaptations. A low cost is not an earthworks, bridge-strength or traffic assessment.
A crossing must be an accepted object
Streets and roads must not cross water merely because a segment looks short. Bridges and other accepted crossings form part of the context passed to the town.
A town’s shape and its tissue are separate.

The engine distinguishes urban footprint, growth mechanism, local phases/cultures, and then the street network and blocks. An oval enclosure does not force a circular town; an organic footprint can contain a grid extension. This separation prevents a simple street pattern from determining the entire geography.

, converting hectares into m². An artistic budget may instead start from a radius. In demographic mode, radius does not act as a second budget. Planned foundations use area-calibrated vector templates; accessibility-driven growth and organic nuclei use a local anisotropic arrival field bounded to 192².

Cost combines relief, travel gradient, access and spatial noise. Cohesion, satellites, branch depth and gap scale control dispersion. A cell reached by propagation is not necessarily allocated to the town. Small pockets that cannot be served may be discarded, leaving the budget unmet. Nuclei separated by water do not implicitly create a bridge.

Regional approaches guide the macroplan. Quarters retain their identities, recipes and phases; computation sectors follow the framework rather than an arbitrary cut at every age boundary. Routing checks gradients along segments. Widths form metric ribbons, rather than merely visible strokes.

Adaptive servicing adds bounded access where a block is too deep for its recipe: corridors must stay inside the parent land, avoid water and neighbours, and respect gradients. This stage belongs to the plan.
Rebuilding parcels retains the streets and blocks
; it must not repair a land deficit by silently moving the network.

Cultures group intentions for morphology, access and architecture. European organic, bastide, medina, Chinese or Japanese plans, communal and fantasy cultures are not synonyms for a perturbed grid. Phase or quarter mixtures remain procedural recipes.
are comparative references: the local code is not presented as their exact solver.
. This screenshot shows a framework and subdivisions; no group of houses is discernible at this scale. It is not evidence of successful built occupation. Provenance and recipe are retained in
Request, reserve, allocate, then count actual results.

The programme receives applied population, settlement role, known resources, cultural context, period, architectural compatibility and lore. It distinguishes domestic, mixed, craft, communal and storage functions, and open space.

. This is not a historical constant. Roles and declarations modulate needs: a crossroads may request more market space; resource-dependent craft may reserve a domain; a harbour requires explicitly declared navigability. Visible water alone does not establish it.

Before cadastral subdivision, the programme reserves existing, served blocks for demanding functions. Geometry and streets are retained. Selection examines dry land, gradients, access contacts and area suitability. Several blocks may contribute to an open-space intention; a single institution is not artificially multiplied to fill a shortfall.

Neighbouring parcels are found through a spatial index, followed by actual collinear boundary overlap. Nearby centroids do not establish adjacency. Allocation ranks demands by candidate scarcity and applies a two-pass greedy heuristic. The second pass may reassign domestic surplus only if the displaced demand remains covered. This is not a global optimum.
Original balance diagram. Units are added only within the same function: market area is not a dwelling count.

Domestic land capacity retains one unit per eligible parcel in the current single-building path. A large parcel does not automatically represent several households. Markets and commons contribute to a separate open-space capacity. Architectural refusals leave real unmet demand; colouring an occupied area on the map does not replace an accepted building.

The automatic density budget may be limited by the cadastral module size: average cultural module area, native minimum and phase shares. The residential-share coefficient (0.65) and shape margin (1.15) are prototype planning assumptions, without demographic certification. Explicit manual overrides retain their role.
A parcel must be accessible and buildable.

Subdivision consumes retained blocks, their holes, reservations and the local recipe. Land-pattern families include frontage, compact tissue, courtyard, communal domain and inherited land. Architectural family is separate: a shared domain may hold individual houses; a stilt site requires native supports.
The engine projects block edges onto street segments. It splits intervals by direction, width and distance, then joins them across successive pieces. Qualification uses the parcel boundary
the block boundary. Duplicates must not artificially increase length. A curve discretised into small segments is not a set of independent accesses.
Tolerances described in the note include a band
, a 14 m distance limit and a 20° angular difference. These are numerical tolerances adapted to existing ribbons, not a cadastral standard.
Original explanatory diagram. An interior centroid guarantees neither building containment nor authorised access.

Strips, oriented cuts and competing frontage territories produce candidates. Witness envelopes must remain contained, including when a hole lies entirely inside a rectangle. Gardens, remnants and reserves retain their identities. An area sum is insufficient: the union must cover the intended parent without overlap and with the same exclusions.

places frontage-constrained subdivision in context. The local competing frontage plans form an oriented-distance partition; they are neither a complete straight skeleton nor the published interactive persistence system.

Admission dimensions come from a versioned table produced by the house engine using solved minimum plans. This boundary reduces inconsistencies between subdivision and architecture. A cadastral witness is nevertheless a search hint: actual placement must still check geometry, access and terrain.
A concrete case: a complete courtyard house is not a shop

The medina note records a souk frontage module of 4.6–6 m, whereas a complete native AF-MAG-B02 courtyard requires approximately 29.62 × 30.67 m before clearance. Imposing that courtyard on every shop creates a domain contradiction. Context selects compatible native sources; it does not illegally shrink a large recipe.
A solved native plan, then physical admission.

The Rust house engine solves a catalogue recipe: bodies, levels, courtyards, circulation, supports, roofs, materials and variants. Cultural mapping is explicit. Similar names do not select a pack at runtime. Strict, inspired and fantasy modes express compatibility policies; “strict” means compliance with the declared recipe ranges, not certification by a historical authority.
Cadastral/buildable polygons and holes, authorised contacts, programme, pack, period, seed and metric ground.
Recipe → admissible parameters → LayoutPlan → volumes, access, levels, supports and actual roof facets.
Containment, overhang rights, neighbours, access connection and ground adaptation. A refusal leaves an explicit deficit.

The automatic workflow may examine up to three pack recipes, with target, intermediate and minimum plans. For a given plan, contacts, positions and setbacks are bounded; the note describes up to 324 transformations per parcel for this path. A specific model chosen in Houses retains its own draw and is not replaced by these automatic alternatives.

Once a plan is solved, candidates apply a rigid transformation. A house that does not fit is not clipped at the boundaries to hide failure. Requested coverage, frontage and depth remain bounded by the recipe and dimension policy. A doorway may be narrower than the body: access and built envelope are separate constraints.
Ground and domain do not come from the image
The supplied ground may be a physical raster with bilinear interpolation. Its origin denotes the centre of the first sample. A local plane
remains a compatibility approximation when used. The displayed terrain texture is not a foundation. A separate domain may authorise roof overhangs; otherwise roofs remain within the cadastre.
Volumes and enrichment share the same plan

The lightweight path produces bodies, levels, supports, an access skeleton and native roof facets. It omits rooms, detailed wall/opening operations and ornament. Detailed enrichment reuses the solved plan instead of drawing a second house. Vertex and index compaction preserves facets without loss; it must not be confused with geometric simplification.

Exterior access constraints and physical surfaces must remain consistent between volumes and detail. Accepted houses, refusals and built capacity are counted after admission, then passed to the programme. A recipe collection or a successful House Bench example does not establish that every town lot can accept a house.

is attached to the stable identity of a native request, inheriting settlement settings for omitted values. Refusals remain visible and retryable. Current replays demonstrate local invalidation, a single house request in their controlled case, and preservation of other houses. Retaining a snapshot and rebuilding from an edited recipe are distinct contracts: these tests alone do not establish exact replay of every override across all backends and editing sequences. Retained neighbours and the reference scene used before overrides must be part of that verification.

To stabilise edit replay, the adapter retains originals only for houses already touched. It restores a reference scene without duplicating the entire scene, then reapplies the current overrides in stable site order. Retained neighbouring buildings become binding occupations for subsequent requests. More local parameters take precedence; dimensions and storeys remain within source limits. This replay mechanism is a project-specific adaptation, distinct from a general proof of order independence for every possible operation.

The final WASM and native audits exercise a specific case: two storeys globally, three for the settlement, then two for the house. The house setting correctly takes precedence; a four-storey request incompatible with the source is refused. The field
records replay of that case’s interactive edits from its recipe, and
checks that refusals belonging to a downstream product are not attributed to an earlier stopping stage. This targeted success does not generalise to every catalogue and editing sequence.

The countryside retains a TypeScript path adapted to Rust site data. Geography, culture and applied context guide land use. Explicit agricultural profiles may request farms on actual rural access routes, outside the retained urban footprint. Programme reservations remain protected; an open growth reserve does not have the same status as a reserved institution.

This pipeline does not compute agricultural yield, food rations or import capacity. A declared resource may have an identified effect in the programme; it does not invent a complete production chain in the countryside.

Render3D vegetation uses a control field in world coordinates: cover, potential height, conifer share and tone/disturbance. The field accounts for climate and topography. Density is transformed in particular by
: this is a cover policy, not a leaf-area measurement.

Riparian galleries have a dedicated envelope tied to visible banks. Tree centres avoid displayed water; crowns may overhang a bank. Using the widened routing mask would produce artificial stepped clearings. At a distance, unresolved cover becomes a material average; up close, crowns become distinguishable. Scale transitions must limit luminance jumps without modifying terrain.
Actual screenshot retained in the documentation campaign

, a 640 m top-down view in the local Godot viewer. This surface path is distinct from web Render3D; it is neither an ecological photograph nor a capture of the latest V2 style. Its original folder contains its manifest and reports.

Elevation-adjusted temperature, rainfall and topographic-position indices serve as proxies. Seasonality, annual snow and materials have their own documented rules. V2 disturbance coefficients are bounded visual policies. They do not describe ecological succession, stand age or observed snow stocks.

Rendering transforms retained data into shaded terrain, materials, water, vegetation, strokes, labels and built geometry. Parchment, Atlas, diagnostic views, Render3D and V2 do not constitute different physical models. Some paths use temporary adapters and rendering; appearance does not guarantee equivalence.
V1: seed 73, requested population 30,000, medina, desert, Atlas. Comparing cultures and styles does not establish their historical fidelity.
Screenshot from the Render3D ground note. The perspective view samples retained terrain; it does not recompute its geology.

Display level of detail may replace a very small roof with a coarse shape and discard off-camera objects. This saves drawing work; the retained native plan remains the architectural authority. An image’s pixel count is neither drainage resolution nor elevation-field resolution.

Materials and canopy have their own spatial scales. A fine texture does not turn a DEM with cells tens of metres wide into centimetre-level topographic measurements. A 3D drawing surface is not the foundation ground, and camera vertical exaggeration must not contaminate physical dimensions.
In the inspected Rust urban V2 integration, the snapshot retains the native scene while its projection to

classifies roofs into display categories such as flat, dome, conical, hip, pagoda and gable. This projection is not an exact rendering of every native facet on the map. “Native geometry retained” and “native geometry fully drawn” require different evidence.

Brushes may be guided by land-use polygons and their holes, with world-anchored candidates and deterministic hashes. Classification uses a spatial index followed by an exact point-in-polygon test. Anchors are constrained; a painted motif’s edges may extend beyond them. Missing occupation data must not invent a forest.

The illustration module transforms a screenshot using a local or external image model and retains a recipe. This image is an interpretation, distinct from the procedural world and its metrics. It must not be used as evidence of a roof, road or house absent from the retained scene.

SVG/PNG describe a view or visible layers; JSON, decors and snapshots may retain the scene and applied settings. Format and workflow determine what can actually be imported again. Parameter URLs do not necessarily replace an imported raster, an applied scene or neural weights. To archive evidence, retain the content, its fingerprints and the recipe, rather than a URL alone.

The backend is part of the recipe.
Browser CPU, using workers where available.
Reference pipeline and adapters; V1 development does not require Rust compilation.
Compiled core exposed through numerical bridges and workers. WASM does not automatically enable the GPU.
Selected terrain and drainage passes; adapter availability and limits must be checked.
Dedicated inference; allocation, transfers and precision contribute to the cost.
Rust on the machine, with a computation API.
Urban/house operations and other capabilities declared by the service. Inspect actual capabilities instead of assuming every endpoint exists.
A separate path with its own models and GPU memory; no bitwise equivalence with the browser is promised.
Local application and associated services, depending on configuration.
A desktop shell alone does not change the core’s methods, precision or limitations.

The Rust core is independent of the browser and renderer; WASM crates expose its functions; bridges and interfaces transport results. Procedural shaders are not neural networks. CPU and GPU may each accelerate one subproblem while another stage remains dominant.

from 28 October obtained finite heights with Rust/WASM CPU, procedural WebGPU terrain, native Rust, Python/CUDA neural generation and WASM/WebGPU neural generation. It retains the announced effective backend, computation provenance, model profiles and identities. These are functional checks of the script’s cases, without guarantees of performance across machines or numerical equivalence between paths.

observed the “Magna Urbis V2” application and its native Rust child service on an available loopback port. The Tauri shell reuses WebView rendering; weights and Python/CUDA remain optional external dependencies. Installers are built for their target system. This Windows check does not certify Linux installation, every GPU driver or neural operation without those dependencies.

A short native computation time is insufficient if transfer or browser preparation blocks. Distinguish cold/warm caches, work required before an image appears and background work. Loading weights, compiling shaders and the selected resolution strongly affect measurements. A small town that does not block does not establish metropolitan-scale performance.
Evidence must identify what it measures.

This delivery checks the documentation page, internal links, local references, images and layout. It does not rerun every native campaign in the project. The measurements below are historical results from method notes, explicitly bounded to their cases; they are not presented as new benchmarks.

retains source paths, collection dates and SHA-256 hashes. Recorded timings are not latency guarantees: the development machine and its caches are shared.

setting, backend, precision, dimensions and any imported raster.
Describe the machine, browser, GPU, caches and initial loading; time stages separately.

Report demand, admissible land, accepted placements, refusals, built/open capacity and deficit, using the units appropriate to each function.
Define the expected criterion before concluding: geometric invariant, deterministic replay, visual quality or performance. None of these criteria replaces all the others.
Two findings to retain, even when uncomfortable

The parcel note reports an initial retained medina with 74 blocks and 72 streets. Correcting a source increased accepted houses from 4 to 148, but built coverage in the core remained 15.9%. This improves recipe consistency; it does not establish a successful dense souk.

An initial complete native case for 50,000 inhabitants produced 6,188 parcels and 5,336 indicative domestic sites for 11,111 requested units. This mismatch motivated recalibration of the automatic budget. A million-inhabitant probe exceeded 240 s and was stopped: no metropolitan performance result is claimed. These figures describe tests preceding later corrections, on the machine used for their review.
Useful commands, to run in their own context
Rust commands require the repository’s toolchain and dependencies. Native replay scripts require a current executable build: an old binary cannot measure a recent source change. Directories such as
are often ignored; a path mentioned in a note may be missing from another checkout.
Which invariants should each stage test?
Finite values, units, support and continuity; preservation when the camera changes.
No loops, consistent levels, connected confluences, corrections within budget.
Connections, gradients, obstacles, authorised crossings and explicit intersections.
Containment, holes, union/coverage, no overlaps, actual access, unchanged streets when recalculating.
Accepted recipe and period, consistent plan/volume/detail, contained roofs and access, physical ground.
Consistent units, refused requests not consumed, open capacity separate from built capacity, real deficits left visible.
The scene actually applied, known camera and scale, no missing layer; explicit visual inspection.
Artistic intensities and bounded corrections; no global geological calibration.
Balances, time units, reference cases and documented sensitivity.
Simplified annual balance; no flood, tide or navigation forecast.
Dedicated time-dependent data and physical validation.
Declared catalogues and influences; parametric recipes rather than universal reconstruction.
Sources contextualised by period/site, comparison with actual plans and specialist review.
Domestic assumptions and indicative densities; land and buildings may fall short.
Counts of accepted buildings, explicit occupation and published deficits.
Bounded placement search; a refusal may indicate search failure or a real incompatibility.
Minimal cases, refusal diagnostics, comparison with a more complete search.
Climate proxies and cover policies; unobserved visual details.
Separate calibration, seasonal variability and an independent corpus.
CPU cost, transfers, memory and rendering not established for every population.
Reproducible end-to-end campaigns, cold/warm caches and failed cases included.
Backend and precision affect outputs; GPU support varies.
Replays across machines, defined tolerances and actual fallback tests.
A snapshot of an active repository; some older screenshots have incomplete provenance.
Revised fingerprints, new capture recipes, and links and claims updated together.

A successful geometric test does not certify urban quality. An attractive screenshot does not certify housing capacity. A native timing does not certify application responsiveness. The project’s value rests on making these distinctions traceable all the way to source code and artifacts.
A few terms, each with one local definition.
Stored elevations and corrections, reused by subsequent stages and views.
Elevation samples on a grid; interpolation does not create newly observed data.
Upstream surface whose routed flow contributes to a cell or reach.
The elevation and ordering required for routing; distinct from physically corrected ground.
Having a cost or response that depends on direction.
